vapid.party - Cloudflare Web Push and XMTP alert relay

Base URL:
- https://vapid.party

Runtime:
- Cloudflare Worker, D1, Cloudflare Queue, and one singleton Cloudflare
  Container running a custom Go XMTP v3 SubscribeAll listener.
- No Vercel/Next or PostgreSQL runtime is supported.
- Public health reported deliveryReady=true, listener ready, and bridge synced
  on 2026-07-14.
- A post-deployment real-Chrome canary passed XMTP welcome and group delivery,
  three HMAC epochs, own-message and shouldPush=false suppression, and cleanup.
- Push remains experimental because SubscribeAll has no durable replay cursor;
  restart/disconnect hints can be missed while XMTP client sync remains authoritative.
- Migration 0006 and the general-public app API are deployed in production.
  Converge and pre-provisioned operator contracts remain separate.
- General-public apps support generic Web Push only. Public XMTP enrollment is
  unavailable until installation ownership can be proven cryptographically.

OpenAPI:
- /openapi.yaml

Response shape:
- Success: `{ "success": true, "data": ... }`
- Error: `{ "success": false, "error": "...", "code": "...", "details": ...? }`
- Validation errors use HTTP 422 and include `details.issues[]`.

Public health:
- GET /api/health
- Top-level status only describes the Worker.
- `data.xmtp.deliveryReady` requires a fresh listener heartbeat, connected XMTP
  stream, successful internal delivery probe, and a D1-synchronized bridge with
  zero pending or failed registrations.
- The response never exposes internal URLs, tokens, endpoints, or HMAC keys.

Public app creation (deployed):
- POST /api/apps
- No account, wallet, approval, or API key is required.
- Body: name (required, 1..255), optional description (max 500), optional
  registrable hostname domain, optional leaderboardOptIn (default false).
- The no-store 201 response returns app.id, app.name, app.publicVapidKey,
  app.createdAt, and one appSecret.
- Save appSecret immediately. The raw value is returned once and only its
  SHA-256 digest is stored. Use it as X-API-Key for trusted-server routes.
- Anonymous creation uses high scoped/global per-minute abuse backstops. Client
  scopes are stored as secret-salted hashes, never raw IP addresses.
- Persistent anonymous state has hard service ceilings of 25,000 public apps
  and 250,000 public subscription rows.
- Service backstops admit at most 5,000 anonymous creation attempts, 5,000
  subscription-verification attempts, and 5,000 authenticated public state
  mutations per minute; successful app creation remains capped at 600/minute.

Public generic browser enrollment (deployed):
- GET /api/apps/{appId}/vapid-public-key
- POST /api/apps/{appId}/enrollment-ticket (X-API-Key on trusted server)
- POST /api/apps/{appId}/subscriptions
- DELETE /api/apps/{appId}/subscriptions
- Browser code does not need and must not receive appSecret.
- The trusted app server validates its own user, then posts the exact standard
  PushSubscription to enrollment-ticket. The no-store response contains a
  five-minute stateless bearer token bound to app id, endpoint, keys, and
  expiration; no ticket state is persisted.
- The browser POSTs that same PushSubscription with the ticket as Authorization
  Bearer. It cannot set userId, channelId, or metadata; the app maps the returned
  subscription id itself. Only canonical FCM, Mozilla, Apple, and WNS endpoints
  are accepted.
- A successful create/refresh returns a new 256-bit management.token and its
  deletePath in a no-store response; only the token hash is stored.
- DELETE body is `{ "endpoint": "..." }` and requires
  `Authorization: Bearer <management.token>`.
- Endpoint keys are immutable while active. Public mutation limits and the
  public app maximum of 150 active physical subscriptions is enforced.
- expirationTime must be null or a future Unix-millisecond timestamp.

General-public XMTP enrollment (unavailable/planned):
- POST /api/apps/{appId}/xmtp/subscriptions
- DELETE /api/apps/{appId}/xmtp/subscriptions
- Public-app credentials receive HTTP 403 on POST/DELETE
  /api/xmtp/registrations and on the app-scoped XMTP status/test paths.
- An appSecret proves control of the vapid.party app, not ownership of a claimed
  XMTP installation. General-public XMTP enrollment remains planned until a
  cryptographic installation-ownership proof contract exists.
- Existing Converge compatibility and pre-provisioned operator XMTP flows are
  separate and remain available according to their rollout status.

App-secret management routes (deployed):
- GET /api/apps/{appId}/stats
- PATCH /api/apps/{appId}/profile
- GET /api/apps/{appId}/domain
- POST /api/apps/{appId}/domain/verify
- POST /api/apps/{appId}/secret/rotate
- DELETE /api/apps/{appId}
- All require X-API-Key: appSecret, and the credential must match appId.
- PATCH accepts name, description, domain or null, and leaderboardOptIn. Set and
  verify the domain before enabling leaderboardOptIn.
- Secret rotation atomically revokes the old secret, returns one new raw secret,
  and is limited to ten rotations per UTC day. App deletion cascades its
  credentials and app-owned state.

DNS and leaderboard (deployed):
- GET /api/leaderboard is public, opt-in, cached for 60 seconds, and returns at
  most 50 apps.
- Publish TXT `_vapid-party.<domain>` with the exact value
  `v=vapid-party1;app=<appId>;vapid=<current-public-vapid-key>`.
- GET /api/apps/{appId}/domain returns the exact record; POST .../domain/verify
  checks it. A listing requires a successful check within seven days and a
  VAPID snapshot matching the current app key.
- Ranking uses providerAcceptedLast7Days across today and the prior six UTC
  dates. Provider accepted does not mean delivered, displayed, or read.
- domainVerifiedAt means last verified. DNS is checked on demand, not monitored
  continuously, so it is not a claim of continuous or current ownership.

Private stats semantics (deployed):
- todayUtc is the current UTC date; last7DaysUtc is today plus six prior UTC dates.
- queued means a recipient job was enqueued.
- providerAccepted means a Web Push provider accepted a send attempt.
- failed counts failed send attempts, including retries.
- expired counts terminal invalid-endpoint outcomes.
- Counters exclude diagnostic tests, retain eight UTC dates, and contain no
  notification payload, endpoint, user, topic, inbox, or message data.

Public Converge XMTP routes:
- GET /api/xmtp/vapid-public-key
- POST /api/xmtp/subscriptions
- DELETE /api/xmtp/subscriptions
- POST /api/xmtp/status
- POST /api/xmtp/status/test

Converge registration:
- No client secret or X-API-Key.
- Version is 1 and app.id must be `converge.cv`.
- Identity contains a 64-hex inboxId and 64-hex installationId. An optional
  address is accepted for wire compatibility but is not needed for routing.
- Subscription is a standard browser PushSubscription.
- Group topics are `/xmtp/mls/1/g-<32 lowercase hex>/proto` and require HMAC keys.
- Welcome topic is `/xmtp/mls/1/w-<64 lowercase hex>/proto` and has no HMAC key.
- Include every backing DM/group topic and every current HMAC epoch from XMTP.
- notification.inboxHandle is an opaque base64url local-routing token, never a
  display name or raw inbox id.
- preferences.minimalPayloadOnly must be true.
- preferences.plaintextPreview must be false.
- Only the strict nested version-1 body is public; flattened legacy bodies fail.
- Browser endpoints are restricted to canonical HTTPS FCM, Mozilla autopush,
  Apple Web Push, and WNS shapes.
- Maximums: 400 topics, 800 combined topic/HMAC rows, 1024 characters per
  base64 key, 1..256 decoded HMAC-key bytes, and uint32 epochs. Listener state
  is capped at 5,000 combined topic/HMAC rows per app and 25,000 globally.
- One inbox identity exists per app/installation. Active endpoint
  p256dh/auth keys are immutable, though several logical routes can share them.
- Send X-Vapid-Party-Diagnostics: 1 to receive a random 256-bit management
  receipt in the no-store response. The server stores only its hash.
- Send the receipt only as Authorization: Bearer. Endpoint replacement and
  post-bootstrap deletion require it; replacement preserves it for safe retry.
- Exact endpoint/key refresh can bootstrap or recover a receipt for deployed
  client compatibility.
- POST /api/xmtp/status has an empty body and returns secret-free route coverage,
  listener/bridge readiness, and delivery stages.
- POST /api/xmtp/status/test queues only `{type:"vapid.diagnostic",testId}`.
  `sent` means provider accepted, not that the browser displayed it.
- First public claim is not signed XMTP ownership proof and can be squatted for
  denial of service. This route is Converge-only, not general app enrollment.

Authenticated app routes:
- Legacy pre-provisioned apps and, after rollout, publicly created apps use
  X-API-Key on trusted servers for generic Web Push.
- GET /api/vapid/public-key
- POST /api/subscribe
- POST /api/send
- Pre-provisioned operator apps may also use:
- POST /api/xmtp/registrations
- DELETE /api/xmtp/registrations
- POST /api/apps/{appId}/xmtp/status
- POST /api/apps/{appId}/xmtp/status/test
- Public-app credentials receive HTTP 403 on the XMTP registration routes.
  General-public XMTP enrollment is not shipped.
- For operator apps, the API key selects app scope; the registration request
  cannot override it.
- Operator registration returns a diagnostic receipt and app-scoped status/test
  paths. Both X-API-Key and Authorization: Bearer <receipt> are required, and
  the receipt is checked against the app id in the path.
- POST /api/send applies per-minute and daily limits to selected recipient
  deliveries, not only request count. Every send is capped at 100 selected
  recipients, including filter-based sends.
- Public apps share service backstops of 2,000 selected recipient deliveries per
  minute and 100,000 per UTC day.
- The serialized notification payload is capped at 3,000 UTF-8 bytes. All jobs
  must fit one estimated 240,000-byte JSON Queue batch and publish through one
  sendBatch; Queue publication failure rolls back the new attempt rows/counters.
- The old wallet-admin routes remain removed and return 404.

Listener delivery:
- POST /api/internal/xmtp/deliveries
- Requires Authorization: Bearer INTERNAL_INGEST_TOKEN.
- Production Container sends a minimal version-1 event with idempotencyKey,
  installationId, opaque app deliveryToken, topic, messageType, shouldPush, and
  isSilent.
- The previous official HTTP SendRequest and legacy internal path/header remain
  transitional compatibility inputs.
- The relay never needs an HMAC secret in the delivery request.

XMTP Web Push payload:
- type: `xmtp.new_message`
- inboxHandle: opaque local routing token
- No title, body, URL, conversation id, sender, preview, ciphertext, or message content.
- The receiving app owns notification copy, navigation, XMTP sync, and decryption.

Privacy:
- vapid.party stores routing metadata and Web Push material needed for delivery.
- It never stores, forwards, or previews plaintext XMTP text, sender names,
  decrypted content, attachment URLs, previews, or encrypted envelopes.
- D1 delivery-attempt rows store no generic or XMTP notification payload. The
  opaque inboxHandle remains registration routing state, but is not copied into
  attempt payloads. Generic copy is transient in Queue/Web Push because it is
  the requested notification; XMTP uses only the minimal wake-up payload there.
- D1 operational rows retain coarse status/timestamps under short retention;
  only diagnostic rows may retain a short-lived testId. Source and dead-letter
  Queue windows can occur sequentially; each must be verified at one hour before launch,
  this requires a Cloudflare plan that permits a 3,600-second setting.
